claims.text: The use of a serum-cholesterol-lowering diet lowers serum cholesterol levels in hospitalized middle-aged men.
The incidence of coronary heart disease during serum-cholesterol-lowering diet periods was about half that during normal-diet periods.
Changes in potential confounding variables were small and failed to account for the reduction in coronary heart disease incidence.
A serum-cholesterol-lowering diet exerts a substantial preventive effect on coronary heart disease.

evidence.description: The use of the SCL diet was associated with markedly lowered serum-cholesterol-values.

The incidence of CHD, as measured by the appearance of certain electrocardiographic patterns and by the occurrence of coronary deaths, was in both hospitals during the SCL-diet periods about half that during the normal-diet periods.
An examination of a number of potential confounding variables indicated that the changes in them were small and failed to account for the considerable reduction in the incidence of CHD.
It is concluded that the use of the serum-cholesterol-lowering diet exerted a substantial preventive effect on CHD.

methodologies.name: Crossover Controlled Intervention Trial
methodologies.description: A 12-year controlled trial in two mental hospitals with a diet reversal (crossover) after six years comparing a serum-cholesterol-lowering diet to a normal hospital diet.
conditions: SCL diet low in saturated fats and cholesterol and relatively high in polyunsaturated fats

limitations.text: The study population was restricted to hospitalized middle-aged men.
